042589143101d02b: WASHINGTON: Former US president Barack Obama has condemned the Trump administration's actions against Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar as an attempt at intimidation following a raid on her home.

"It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can't selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say," Obama wrote on X on Sunday, reported German news agency dpa.
"But that's exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota."
Obama is known for carefully weighing which current political events he comments on.

In his lengthy post, he complained that the government was actively trying to deport the Somalia-born Trump critic, "seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalised, and therefore is not a citizen."
Under US citizenship rules, it makes a difference whether someone is under 18 or not.
Had Omar been 18 at the time of her father's naturalisation, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately, Obama noted.
"But because she was 17, she became a naturalised citizen automatically."
The first Black US president was once confronted with the false claim, prominently promoted by Trump, that he had been born in Kenya rather than in the US state of Hawaii.
Last Monday, federal agents searched Omar's home in the Washington area.
The move drew heavy criticism, partly because of its timing shortly before the congressional elections, in which the congresswoman is seeking re-election.
ea38a7a6bf3e1f7d: VIVIENNE Westwood creative director Andreas Kronthaler says the fashion industry is in a "precarious moment" as he unveiled his latest Spring-Summer collection for the British house at Paris Fashion Week.

Kronthaler, the Austrian widower of Vivienne Westwood who took over after her death, found inspiration from African fabrics and his own penchant for night gowns for the typically whimsical designs of his SS27 collection called "Body and Soul".

A piece of African fabric bought at the Barbes market in Paris was one starting point, as was his decision to start wearing his night gown outside in the street during this summer's searing heatwaves.
"I just lived my life in it, and I went on my bicycle and shopping and what not. And people really liked it," he told AFP. "And I thought that's nice, my life shirt."

'Orange Is the New Black' actress Natasha Lyonne headed down the catwalk wearing an animal print jacket with nothing underneath, as former supermodel Heidi Klum and actresses Rose McGowan and Paris Jackson looked on from the front row.
Asked about the commercial environment for fashion labels, with many creative directors under pressure, Kronthaler acknowledged the generally difficult trading conditions.

"We (Vivienne Westwood) are independent, and there are good sides to this, and of course there are hard sides to this. But it's okay," he told AFP. "We are living in a very precarious moment because things are not so secure in fashion."

Several top designers from Anthony Vaccarello at Saint Laurent, Pierpaolo Piccioli at Balenciaga and Chemena Kamali at Chloe have been linked to possible exits in recent news reports, although none of the labels have commented publicly.

Elsewhere on Saturday, French luxury house Hermes presented its women's collection in the courtyard of the elite Republican Guard police unit in Paris, making the zip its leitmotif and the ultra-fine strap an accessory.
Zips were used to modulate the length of the skirts, they ran across leather jackets and down a flared blue pair of trousers.

The family-controlled maker of the famous Kelly bag, which generates nearly half of its sales from leather goods and saddlery, is also going through a rough patch, even though it is holding up better than the rest of the sector.
On July 29, the group saw its share price plunge by as much as 11 per cent during the session on the day it released its half-year results. Shares are down 39 per cent since the start of the year.
Chief womenswear designer Nadege Vanhee will present the brand's first haute couture collection in January during Paris Couture Week.
At the same time, British designer Grace Wales Bonner will make her runway debut as artistic director of Hermes menswear.
4bcc21d99044bd23: KUALA LUMPUR: National junior hockey coach Nor Saiful Zaini has urged his players to be more clinical up front when they face Japan in their second Sultan of Johor Cup match at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium tomorrow.
Malaysia opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over China on Sunday, while Japan thrashed Canada 8-1.
Nor Saiful, who has targeted a top-three finish in the Under-21 tournament, said he was dissatisfied with his team's finishing in their opening fixture.
"The players need to be more clinical, especially against a very good Japanese side. We need a win over Japan to stay in contention for a podium finish.

"Japan have shown that they are title contenders by outplaying Canada in their first match. Japan have brought new players here as they had a different team during last month's Junior Asia Cup," he said.
Nor Saiful noted that Japan are a strong side with a disciplined structure and fast attacking play.
"They even have three players who will join the senior team for the Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab, India, from Oct 27-Nov 5.
"It will be a challenge for my forwards to break into their semi-circle to score. Our players need to play a very disciplined game as Japan have a good structure.
The Japanese overall are good in every department, and they play a fast attacking game," he said.
He added that the bouncy pitch at Taman Daya should not affect the players and picked Japan as one of the favourites to win the tournament.

Tomorrow's fixtures: Canada vs China (5pm), Japan vs Malaysia (7.30pm)

ab08803a44c3238c: PETALING JAYA: Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) akan memulakan siasatan terhadap pengurusan, tadbir urus kewangan dan pelaksanaan fizikal projek Lebuhraya Pan Borneo (LPB) Sabah Fasa 1 susulan beberapa kelemahan dibangkitkan dalam Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (LKAN) 2/2026.

Pengerusinya Mas Ermieyati Samsudin berkata PAC akan meneliti secara mendalam bagaimana masalah itu boleh berlaku walaupun pelbagai jawatankuasa pemantauan telah diwujudkan di peringkat negeri dan Persekutuan.
Menurutnya, PAC akan memanggil saksi daripada Kementerian Kerja Raya, Jabatan Kerja Raya (JKR), termasuk JKR Sabah, serta agensi dan pihak berkaitan untuk memberi keterangan dalam prosiding itu.

"Sekiranya prosiding menemukan sebarang indikasi salah laku, rasuah atau penyelewengan kuasa, PAC tidak akan teragak-agak merujuk dapatan berkenaan kepada Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) dan polis untuk siasatan lanjut.

“PAC komited untuk menjalankan siasatan ini secara bebas, telus dan menyeluruh demi memastikan setiap sen wang rakyat dibelanjakan secara berhemah, bertanggungjawab dan mematuhi peraturan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Mas Ermieyati berkata PAC memandang serius penemuan audit berkaitan projek itu, khususnya membabitkan kelewatan, pengurusan projek, pematuhan peraturan kewangan serta jumlah wang awam yang telah dibelanjakan.
"Keadaan itu lebih ketara apabila dibandingkan dengan LPB Sarawak Fasa 1 yang telah siap dibina walaupun kedua-dua projek dimulakan sekitar tempoh sama," katanya.
Projek LPB Sabah Fasa 1 sepanjang 706km melibatkan 35 pakej kerja dan pada asalnya sepatutnya dilaksanakan dalam tempoh 69 bulan serta siap sepenuhnya pada hujung 2021.

Bagaimanapun, hanya empat daripada 35 pakej atau 11.4% telah disiapkan, manakala baki 31 pakej bernilai RM16.319 bilion masih dalam pelaksanaan walaupun projek itu sepatutnya siap kira-kira lima tahun lalu.
Daripada jumlah itu, sembilan pakej dikategorikan sebagai projek sakit dan 13 mengalami kelewatan daripada jadual ditetapkan, manakala sembilan lagi mendahului jadual.
LKAN turut mendapati unjuran kos semasa bagi 15 pakej kerja Fasa 1A meningkat RM987 juta atau 9.5% kepada RM11.323 bilion berbanding kos siling asal RM10.336 bilion.
64e2678a08a83898: ADDIS ABABA: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has reaffirmed its continued support to Kenya following the confirmation of four additional Ebola cases, bringing the country's total caseload to seven, reported Xinhua.

Kenya's ministry of health on Saturday confirmed that all four new cases were detected among individuals already under quarantine following exposure to the initial case, as efforts to prevent community transmission of the haemorrhagic fever gather momentum.

In a statement issued late Saturday, the Africa CDC said that Kenya's early identification demonstrates the critical role of contact tracing, surveillance, and timely isolation in interrupting transmission and protecting communities.

The African Union's specialised continental public health agency also commended the Kenyan authorities for their "leadership, swift public health measures and transparent communication throughout the response."

"Africa CDC stands firmly alongside the government and people of Kenya, healthcare workers and all those affected by this outbreak," it said. "Protecting lives requires sustained vigilance, public trust, community engagement and coordinated action."

Noting that the evolving Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reinforces the urgency of strong regional preparedness, the Africa CDC called on countries and partners to strengthen cross-border surveillance, information sharing, early detection and coordinated public health action across the continent.
The agency further encouraged communities to remain vigilant, follow guidance from national health authorities, and report symptoms promptly.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person, or through contaminated materials. Early detection and access to appropriate care improve the chances of survival and help prevent further transmission, it said.
b86582990723b719: KUALA LUMPUR: Mental health issues among workers are recognised by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) through three financial assistance avenues: the Invalidity Pension, the Invalidity Scheme, and the Employment Injury Scheme.

Perkeso deputy chief executive officer (operations) Azirruan Arifin said psychiatric and mental health conditions are approved as invalidities every year, enabling eligible contributors to receive related benefits, including a monthly Invalidity Pension.

He said contributors facing mental health issues that result in an inability to work qualify for the monthly Invalidity Pension, while conditions evaluated under the Invalidity Scheme include major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and severe anxiety disorders.
"If the condition causes infirmity that affects a person's capacity to work, it can be assessed for invalidity benefits, subject to evaluation by the Perkeso Medical Board and prescribed conditions.

"Mental health disorders stemming from workplace trauma, such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), can be considered under the Employment Injury Scheme if there is clinical confirmation, a clear link to employment, and medical assessment," he told Berita Harian.

He added that official records show psychiatric and mental health cases are certified and approved as invalidities annually, giving eligible contributors access to Invalidity Scheme benefits and medical treatment facilities.
"This shows that mental health issues have a direct impact on an individual's ability to work, and when invalidity criteria are met, they can be evaluated within Perkeso's social security framework.
"Medical and psychiatric evaluations are crucial in helping the Perkeso Medical Board determine the severity of the illness and its impact on the contributor's work capacity," he said.
Azirruan noted that contributors undergoing invalidity assessment must receive appropriate treatment and medical monitoring to allow for a comprehensive health evaluation.

For certain cases, a minimum monitoring and treatment period of one year is required before an assessment can be made, allowing medical experts to evaluate disease progression, response to treatment, and recovery levels.
"This is also essential to determine whether the health condition has reached Maximum Medical Improvement (MMI) and if the infirmity is permanent enough to impair the contributor's ability to work.
"However, decisions regarding invalidity remain subject to medical evaluations and rulings by the Perkeso Medical Board based on the facts of each case," he said.
He emphasised that mental health is a critical workplace issue today due to evolving pressures and environments that differ significantly from those faced in the past.
He added that Perkeso actively participates in promotional efforts to help organisations address workplace mental health.

"Under the Employment Injury Scheme, mental health conditions resulting from workplace trauma, such as PTSD, can be considered if supported by clinical confirmation from a psychiatrist and a clear connection to job-related events," he said.
8c807a5178382cbc: MEDICAL overtreatments are an unresolved concern in our society and contribute to patient injury and increased costs.
You have a good family insurance package, so why not just remove the thyroid or go through a thyroidectomy?
Those words, spoken casually by an endocrinologist during a consultation for simple, benign nodules, continue to linger in my mind.

The suggestion that my brother and I undergo major organ removal and become dependent on thyroxine (levothyroxine) for the rest of our lives, not out of clinical necessity, but because our insurance coverage could absorb the claim, was deeply unsettling.
It offered a direct look into a concerning trend in modern healthcare: insurance policies leveraging unnecessary surgical procedures.

Beyond the immediate ethical concern, it raises a critical legal question regarding where profit-driven overtreatment moves from a breach of medical ethics into medical negligence or gross negligence under Malaysian tort law.

In medical jurisprudence, distinguishing between ordinary negligence and gross negligence remains a challenging issue for the courts. While both exist on a spectrum of clinical error, they differ in intent, degree, and standard of care.

Ordinary medical negligence occurs when a healthcare provider makes an honest mistake or fails to provide the standard of care expected of a reasonably competent professional in similar circumstances.

It is an objective failure, such as misreading a lab result, misinterpreting an imaging scan, or missing a diagnostic sign during a busy shift. While the outcomes can be tragic, the underlying act stems from human error or systemic oversight.
Gross negligence involves a far greater departure from standard practice. It requires a conscious, voluntary act or omission in reckless disregard of a legal duty and patient safety.

It represents a significant indifference to care, such as operating under the influence, performing procedures on the wrong surgical site, or recommending invasive surgeries for benign conditions primarily for financial gain.

In medical malpractice litigation, events are examined after a poor outcome has occurred. A series of minor misjudgements can appear reckless in hindsight, even if individual choices seemed reasonable to the practitioner at the time.

Standard negligence requires proving a failure to meet objective clinical standards. Gross negligence often requires establishing a practitioner's state of mind, demonstrating that they consciously disregarded known risks or prioritised financial gain over patient safety.

Proving subjective intent within a complex medical record is difficult. Modern healthcare delivery involves multiple personnel and administrative processes. When harm occurs, or unnecessary procedures are advised, liability can be spread across hospital protocols, billing practices, and clinical teams, making individual accountability hard to pinpoint.
Defensive medicine further complicates the landscape, contributing to excessive testing that physicians believe may discourage medical malpractice lawsuits.

Excessive healthcare spending is likely to continue as long as physicians' concern about medical liability leads to ordering additional tests to avoid a missed diagnosis or interventions to prevent poor outcomes.
Recommending the surgical removal of an organ when benign nodules could be safely monitored with periodic ultrasound scans violates the core medical duty to avoid unnecessary harm.

Despite ultrasound scans and biopsies, inducing fear in patients also constitutes medical negligence. Performing an unnecessary surgery can constitute medical negligence, even if the patient underwent standard pre-operative testing and signed a consent form.

When medical recommendations are influenced by insurance payouts rather than clinical necessity, patients face real risks, including anaesthetic complications, lifelong hormone dependency, nerve injury, and difficult surgical recovery without clinical benefit.

Furthermore, ordinary negligence usually leads to civil claims covered by medical defence insurance, whereas gross negligence can result in criminal investigations, punitive damages, and disciplinary action by professional regulators.

International precedents highlight the severity of this issue. In 2012, Louisiana cardiologist Dr Mehmood Patel was criminally charged and convicted of performing unnecessary coronary stent placement and balloon angioplasty procedures after having been the highest-billing interventional cardiologist in the state.

Similarly, in United States vs McLean, a busy cardiologist was convicted of fraud for placing coronary stents in vessels with only 50 per cent blockages, where government experts established that at least a 70 per cent blockage was required to justify the procedure.

In 2015, an Indiana family successfully sued a now-deceased orthopaedic surgeon for performing an unnecessary distal clavicle resection on their 16-year-old wrestler son after an expert medical panel confirmed the operation was unwarranted.

Ensuring patient protection requires strict oversight from regulatory bodies such as the Malaysian Medical Council and clear standards from the judiciary. Medical decisions must remain centred on clinical necessity rather than commercial opportunity.
When clinical recommendations are shaped by insurance limits rather than patient health, it represents a breakdown in the duty of care that demands strict accountability.
Head, School of Law Enforcement, Malaysia University of Science and Technology (MUST)

36d21e2445a0455b: KOTA KINABALU: Dua beranak maut selepas kereta dinaiki mereka dihempap sebuah kontena dan lori treler yang terbalik dalam kemalangan di Jalan Pelabuhan Sepanggar Bay, berhampiran Wisma Sabah Ports malam tadi.
Mangsa yang maut ialah pemandu kenderaan serba guna (MPV), Mohd Jadi Pelbi, 53, bersama dengan anak perempuannya yang berada di tempat duduk penumpang Norfaieza Mohd Jadi, 24.
Pusat Gerakan Operasi Jabatan Bomba Sabah memaklumkan menurut keterangan saksi, lori treler berkenaan sedang menjalankan kerja menaikkan sebuah kontena di tepi jalan utama ke atas treler.
“Ia hilang keseimbangan lalu terbalik menghempap kenderaan mangsa yang sedang melalui jalan berkenaan.
“Sebanyak 26 anggota bersama pelbagai jentera bergegas ke lokasi kejadian sejauh 25km sejurus menerima panggilan kecemasan pada 6.31 petang,” menurut kenyataan Pusat Gerakan Operasi itu.

Menurutnya, operasi menyelamat mangsa yang tersepit di dalam kereta itu memerlukan bantuan dua buah kren daripada syarikat lori terbabit yang tiba di tapak kejadian pada 9.21 malam bagi mengangkat muatan kontena berkenaan.
Pasukan penyelamat kemudian bertindak mengeluarkan kedua-dua mangsa yang tersepit menggunakan peralatan pemotong hidraulik khas sejurus bebanan kontena dialihkan daripada kenderaan terbabit.

Kedua-dua mangsa bagaimanapun disahkan meninggal dunia di tempat kejadian akibat kecederaan parah oleh pegawai perubatan Kementerian Kesihatan yang berada di lokasi sebelum mayat dua beranak itu diserahkan kepada pihak polis bagi tindakan lanjut serta urusan bedah siasat.
Operasi menyelamat yang turut dibantu 17 anggota polis ditamatkan sepenuhnya pada 10.30 malam selepas keadaan di kawasan perindustrian itu disahkan selamat daripada sebarang bahaya lain.

Sementara itu Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Sabah dan Sarawak) Mustafa Sakmud berkata pihak yang didapati culas dan gagal mematuhi piawaian keselamatan pengendalian kontena sehingga mengorbankan dua beranak di Jalan Sepanggar petang semalam itu, akan dipertanggungjawabkan.

Beliau yang juga Ahli Parlimen Sepanggar menggesa polis dan pihak berkuasa menjalankan siasatan menyeluruh bagi mengenal pasti punca sebenar insiden maut itu, khususnya membabitkan tatacara keselamatan operasi kenderaan berat di kawasan berkenaan.

“Jika ada elemen culas dan ‘non-compliance’ yang melibatkan mana-mana pihak, saya akan pastikan mereka yang terlibat dipertanggungjawabkan kerana cukuplah insiden kemalangan melibatkan kenderaan berat ini berulang di Sepanggar.

“Sebagai seorang ayah, luluh hati saya menerima perkhabaran mengenai tragedi menyayat hati ini dan keutamaan kita adalah memastikan keluarga mangsa mendapat pembelaan serta sokongan sewajarnya," katanya menerusi hantaran di laman Facebook.
Mustafa turut merakamkan ucapan takziah kepada seluruh keluarga mangsa yang maut dalam kejadian itu.

Bagi membela nasib waris terjejas, beliau mengarahkan Pusat Khidmat Parlimen Sepanggar (Suara Sepanggar) menziarahi keluarga mangsa bagi mengenal pasti keperluan mendesak di samping membantu menyemak serta menguruskan sebarang bentuk bantuan dan pampasan yang layak diterima.
80c3c69728de495d: SINGAPORE: Indonesian stocks slid to a six-year low on Monday as a warning from MSCI over possible expulsion from its global indexes next year rattled fragile investor sentiment, sharpening the focus on how Jakarta intends to allay the index provider's concerns.

Jakarta's benchmark stocks fell over five per cent in early trading on Monday after plunging 11.6 per cent on Friday, as the world's worst performers reeled from index provider MSCI saying it was considering shifting Indonesia to "standalone" status from its current "emerging markets" mantle.

A shift to standalone status would risk cutting Southeast Asia's biggest economy off from international capital, relegate it to an investment backwater and club it with a group of standalone markets that includes Lebanon and Zimbabwe.
The more-severe-than-expected move has raised the stakes for Indonesia's regulators and finance officials.

On Monday, the Indonesia Stock Exchange said it cut its lower auto-rejection limit to seven per cent from 15 per cent to give investors "an opportunity to evaluate and digest available information, helping them make better investment decisions based on Indonesia's economic fundamentals".
The move followed a weekend meeting between the financial regulator and capital market participants, including analysts and economists.

An Indonesian regulator on Friday also unveiled sanctions against those linked to alleged trading manipulation in shares of three firms, with the fines totalling 2.1 trillion rupiah (US$116.4 million).

Angus Mackintosh, an Asean specialist at Aletheia Capital in Singapore, said the fact the fines were announced on Friday suggests that Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has been working on the matter for a while.

"The fines are a positive move, but there needs to be concerted action to stamp the authority of the OJK and take direct action against certain well-known players who have been involved in market abuse," he said.

MSCI had threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status in January because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour but said on Friday the lack of progress in remedying those concerns meant even a drop to that status would not reflect the severity of the issues.

"The burden of proof has shifted: avoiding reclassification will require clear evidence that the announced reforms have been consistently implemented and materially improved market functioning," strategists at Goldman Sachs said in a note.
WIDER RISKS FROM MSCI'S WARNING

Goldman Sachs estimates a full MSCI removal could trigger US$5.6 billion of passive outflows. Active funds benchmarked to these indexes hold more than US$8 billion, although any selling would be discretionary rather than benchmark-driven, they wrote.
Foreign investors have net sold US$4.88 billion worth of Indonesian stocks so far this year, on track for the biggest annual outflow in at least 16 years.
Aninda Mitra, head of Asia macro and investment strategy at BNY Investments, said foreign equity exposure to Indonesia has shrunk to the point where "there may not be much more downside from here."
"But at the same time, even if there are some interesting and fundamentally sound companies and banks, attracting sufficiently large amounts of capital will be tougher in this environment," he said.

MSCI's warning raises the stakes for the government of President Prabowo Subianto, which has faced a series of setbacks this year, with Moody's and Fitch having cut their sovereign rating outlooks to negative earlier in 2026.
Investors are also fretting over the ramifications beyond the US$500 billion stock market, with the rupiah weakening to 18,040 per dollar, not far from the record low of 18,190 hit in June.

"Our bigger concern is not index-related selling itself," said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments in Singapore, "but the potential near-term spillover into the rupiah and domestic bond yields, where market dislocation could translate into tighter financial conditions and a more meaningful impact on the real economy."

f66cb73f44ce05b6: KUALA LUMPUR: There have been no delays in payments to contractors working on the Pan Borneo Highway project that could affect construction progress, deputy works minister Ahmad Maslan told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said payments for Phases 1A and 1B are being made in line with physical progress, with disbursements keeping pace with or exceeding scheduled levels.
"Phase 1A, comprising 15 work packages, has achieved 89.54% physical completion against a scheduled 96.23%, while financial disbursements stand at 88.78%.
"For Phase 1B, which only recently began, actual physical progress stands at 25.53%, ahead of the scheduled 24.76%.

"Financial disbursements have reached 22.11%, exceeding the scheduled 20.73%. Therefore, there is no issue with payments," he said in reply to Wetrom Bahanda (KDM-Kota Marudu) on whether delays in the project were caused by late payments to contractors or a lack of expertise in the appointment of contractors.
Ahmad acknowledged that contractor performance must be addressed to keep the project on track.
He said the works ministry had tightened monitoring through monthly meetings to review construction progress and resolve emerging issues.
The meetings, chaired by the Sabah state secretary and the ministry's secretary-general, are part of efforts to ensure the effective implementation of the project, he said.

The ministry has also introduced measures to prevent further delays, including strengthening steering committees and special task forces to assess contractor performance, identify causes of delays and develop solutions.
These measures are aimed at ensuring that the Pan Borneo Highway project is completed on schedule, he said.
8c01ac317cb8dd83: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has warned civil servants against bureaucratic delays, saying the success of the 2027 Budget 2027 hinges on effective implementation rather than policy announcements alone.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said civil servants must ensure government initiatives are executed efficiently, particularly following wage increases, lower petrol prices, and other measures aimed at easing the people's burden.

"If wages have increased, petrol prices have come down, and the economy is in this position, yet we remain ungrateful, work is still sluggish and slow, and a letter that could be answered in one day takes two weeks, that is asking for trouble for the country," he said at the Finance Ministry's monthly assembly here today.
9aa15e35b6fa51a4: PUTRAJAYA: The government still has to bear debts linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), including interest payments, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, dismissed claims that all debts owed by the strategic investment company had been settled.
He said repayments on existing debts must continue despite ongoing government efforts to control new borrowings and reduce the national debt burden through disciplined fiscal management.

"Some say all 1MDB debts have been paid. I don't know what book they read that from, but it is not true. Our debts, including the interest, must be paid," he said during his address at the Finance Ministry's monthly assembly here.

The grand final was held on Saturday. Her prizes include a full higher-education scholarship from Veritas University, a return flight to Japan and RM3,000 in cash.

According to a statement by the organisers, Kavitha said the programme’s community outreach work was the defining part of her experience, giving her a deeper understanding of the importance of giving back to society.

Shajana Vincent from Negeri Sembilan was named first runner-up, followed by Yashwini Ravindranath from Selangor in second place.

99ae3b753c356398: GOMBAK, Oct 19 — Fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) will start from as low as RM60 one way for Economy Transit services between Gombak and KotaSAS or Kota Sultan Ahmad Shah, Kuantan, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said today.

8ee83fe5e3d585bc: SINGAPORE: Muhamad Yasin, a 63-year-old parking attendant in central Jakarta, says he has cut back on meals as rising prices have put food staples beyond his reach.

"I used to be able to get rice, tempeh and tofu for 7,000 to 8,000 rupiah (US$0.39 to US$0.44). Now it's 15,000 rupiah," said Yasin, who earns 200,000 to 300,000 rupiah a week, beside the minimarket where he watches over parked motorcycles.

Global food inflation is poised to accelerate in the coming months and persist well into 2027, as war-related shipping disruptions and El Nino-driven drought squeeze cereal supplies, putting additional pressure on vulnerable consumers like Yasin, a father of four.

In Indonesia, rice prices have already jumped to record highs amid forecasts of delayed rains, while the cost of bread in Egypt has risen by a quarter and sugar prices in India hit an all-time high as the weakest monsoon in over a decade curbed production.
"All this has put considerable pressure on the system," said Maximo Torero, chief economist at the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).
"We will see a bigger impact towards the end of the year, at the beginning of next year and potentially throughout next year."

The world's poorest consumers are being hit the hardest as food prices rise sharply in low- and middle-income countries across the Middle East, North Africa and Asia, where food accounts for a larger share of household spending.
According to the World Bank, food prices in the September quarter outpaced headline inflation in 22% of the 150 countries it analysed, up from 14% in the previous quarter.
The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded commodities, averaged 136 points in September, the highest reading since November 2022.
Rising prices heighten the risk of social unrest and could prompt governments that are key suppliers to impose export bans, further exacerbating shortages.
Multiple supply shocks

Attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure have disrupted wheat shipments, forcing top importers Egypt and Indonesia to seek alternative supplies, while Red Sea insecurity diverts vessels onto longer, costlier routes around Africa.

The US-Israeli war on Iran has raised fuel prices and disrupted fertiliser exports through the Strait of Hormuz, driving up farming costs even as dry El Nino weather reduces output in India and Southeast Asia.

Wheat prices Wv1 are up more than 30% in 2026, while rice prices in key Asian exporting countries have risen 10% to 13% in spite of large inventories. Fertiliser prices are off peaks reached earlier in the Iran war, but they remain elevated.

"Rising inflation, particularly food inflation, is a reality," said Manish Tiwary, chairman and managing director of Nestle India, citing "a challenging environment" that is due in part to higher commodity costs.

In Egypt, prices of unsubsidised bread have risen to around 5 Egyptian pounds (US$0.093) for a big loaf from 4 pounds in July, while the price of cooking oil has climbed about 40% in the United Arab Emirates.
Vegetable oil in Indonesia has jumped 7% this year, even though the country is the world's biggest palm oil producer.
Prices of sugar, onions and pulses in India jumped more than 10% in September from a month earlier due to production shortfalls.
For baker Sayed Abdel Hamid Mohamed in downtown Cairo, it is not just the price of flour.
"If you bring in a skilled worker, it costs you a lot," he said. "Electricity, water, yeast and the materials we use to produce the loaf of bread for consumers have all risen."
Tarek Azab, a customer at the bakery, said prices have been continuously rising, "not once, twice, or three times," in the past few years.
Freight rates have risen about 50% on some key global routes such as the Black Sea to Southeast Asia as oil prices and war premiums surge.
Infation catalyst
While food prices have been rising since late 2025, dwindling local supplies and higher commodity costs feeding through to consumers threaten to accelerate inflation.
Key importers in the Middle East and Africa that held off on buying after strong local harvests now need to return to the world's markets, potentially triggering a surge in demand.

"In a couple of months, there could be a significant new wave of demand as importers return to the market," said Alexander Karavaytsev, a senior economist at the International Grains Council in London.
The cushion from record global grain inventories is wearing thin, the FAO's Torero said.

"Stocks and good harvests in previous seasons have provided a buffer, but those buffers are starting to come under pressure," he said. "That means commodity price increases could become more pronounced."
Food processors that typically buy raw materials on three- to six-month contracts are now renewing those deals at higher prices, with weaker local currencies magnifying the costs.

"Shipping costs have also increased and when converted into rupiah, the impact is amplified by the weakening of the Indonesian currency," said Franciscus Welirang, a director of PT Indofood, the country's largest food company.
On top of higher prices, food processors are experiencing difficulties in securing supplies, traders said.

Several wheat millers in Indonesia are running their units below capacity as the Russia-Ukraine war has reduced cargo arrivals, said a senior executive at a flour milling company in Jakarta who did not want to be named as they were not authorised to speak to the media.
Indonesian wheat arrivals dropped 41% to 491,000 metric tons in September from a year earlier, Kpler data showed.

For now, soybean and corn inventories are ample, with future supplies hinging on production in the US and South America, although higher oil prices LCOc1 have supported both crops because of their growing use in biofuels.

Favourable southern hemisphere wheat harvests are expected and any downside risk to output in exporters like Australia and Argentina could add a new bullish element to prices, the IGC's Karavaytsev said.
"There is significant upside risk in prices," he said.
68d42102b024c992: SANGGAU: Supendi, a 33-year-old palm fruit farmer, cooled his heels at a mill in Indonesia's West Kalimantan for four frustrating days earlier this month trying to unload his harvest of fresh fruit bunches before being told to leave as the site was full.

For several weeks, local palm oil mills have cut their fresh fruit bunch purchases because storage tanks are filled with processed oil they cannot ship out as a prolonged drought driven by "super El Nino" conditions has dried out the area's main transportation artery, the Kapuas River.
"The fruit was not accepted," Supendi told Reuters by telephone. "Now we're at a loss as to how to sell it."

He had driven from his hometown to the Multi Prima Entakai palm oil mill in the city of Sanggau in early October carrying 7 metric tons of fruit bunches from his small farm and neighbouring ones. He is one of thousands of smallholder farmers in West Kalimantan stuck with rotting fruit.
Supendi's struggles illustrate one of the many impacts of this year's extreme El Nino in Indonesia and Southeast Asia.

The weather phenomenon caused by a warming of the Pacific Ocean waters off South America typically causes hot, dry weather in Southeast Asia. But the strength of the current pattern has parched rivers and wells in Indonesia and fanned forest fires in Borneo — where West Kalimantan is located — and Sumatra that have spread choking haze over the province and as far as Malaysia and Singapore.

West Kalimantan accounts for about 11 per cent of palm oil output in Indonesia, the world's largest producer, and analysts estimate fourth-quarter output across Indonesian Borneo could fall by 12 per cent to 15 per cent because of the El Nino-related disruptions.
SANDBANKS AND STRANDED BARGES

The Kapuas — Indonesia's longest river at 1,143km — transports 40 per cent of West Kalimantan's palm oil output, according to data from the Indonesian Palm Oil Association, known as GAPKI. Sandbanks have emerged from the receding waters of the river, causing several barges and tugboats to run aground, according to Reuters witnesses.
Road delivery is a limited alternative, because trucks carry less than barges and fewer are available, millers say.

During El Ninos in 2015 and 2018, similar droughts lasted for about a month, several local farmers said. But this year the Kapuas has dropped to a lower level and the effects have lasted for two months already.

Indonesia's weather agency expects the start of the rainy season to be pushed back to November, from October normally, delaying the river's resurgence and relief from the country's most intense wildfires in 11 years.
OUTPUT IMPACT

Thirteen palm oil mills out of 50 in West Kalimantan have been affected by the transportation disruptions, accounting for roughly half of the province's processing capacity, said Aris Supratman, who heads GAPKI's West Kalimantan office.
He estimated palm oil supply from the province would fall by about 11 per cent in September from August due to the backup.
"Because of the disruption, shipments are being delayed, and once their storage tanks are full, they inevitably have to limit production," he said.
GAPKI has revised down its 2026 national palm oil production forecast by 2.9 per cent as the dry weather slows fruit maturity.

Dian Kurniawan, 44, a manager at the Multi Prima Entakai mill that turned Supendi away, said the company's fruit bunch purchases had dropped to 10,000 tons in September compared to the 30,000 tons it processed in July.
As of Oct 1, the mill held 8,200 tons of crude palm oil, near its storage tank capacity of 8,500 tons.

"We usually can deliver 2,000 tons in four days, but with trucks sometimes we can only deliver 100 tons per day," Dian said, adding that truck shipments are not only slower than by barge but also three times the cost.

Farmers unable to sell their harvests face difficulties maintaining their palm trees, said Indra Rustandi, who heads the West Kalimantan branch of smallholder farmers group APKASINDO, adding the lack of income has caused some to cut their fertiliser applications by up to 70 per cent to save costs.

Another Sanggau smallholder, 63-year-old Rahmat Wiyono, said he struggled to sell his fruit over the last two months, sometimes driving six hours only to be offered 2,650 rupiah (US$0.15) per kg of fruit bunches, compared with three hours to his regular mill, which had paid 3,400 rupiah.

"Some of our friends haven't had any harvest for the past two months, so they have had to find other ways to supplement their daily income," such as selling homemade cakes and donuts, he said.--REUTERS

fe0957f30fb23a6c: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has advised the coalition’s 18 assemblymen in Negeri Sembilan to stay out of matters involving the Dewan Keadilan dan Undangan (DKU) and the royal institution, and instead focus on serving the people.
Zahid said elected representatives should fulfil their mandate by addressing the people’s problems, Utusan Malaysia reported.

"Our position is that we must separate legal issues and the royal institution from matters concerning the administration of state government," the deputy prime minister was quoted as saying after officiating the Road Safety Congress 2026 in Kuala Lumpur.
"That is why my advice to our assemblymen is that they should no longer interfere in DKU matters and the royal institution."
Negeri Sembilan has been embroiled in a royal crisis since April, when four purported undangs, or chieftains, announced the removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state ruler.

They said the crisis must "under no circumstances" be used as a political tool, a means of garnering support, an opportunity to expand influence or a platform for advancing power struggles.
Several videos were later circulated on social media, showing an irate Tuanku Muhriz ticking off menteri besar Ismail Lasim after Friday prayers at a mosque.

In one video, Tuanku Muhriz refused to receive Ismail in audience and alleged that the menteri besar had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal in August to state that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the Yang Dipertuan Besar.

cef1f42eade6d88e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Singer-actress Bella Astillah was moved to tears when her nine-year-old son, Mohamed Ayden Adrean, delivered an emotional speech at her wedding reception with Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman last night.

49cb2b17bc85cfdd: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has welcomed calls to involve members of parliament in implementing the Kampung Angkat Madani programme to ensure it meets community needs.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong told the Dewan Rakyat that under the 2027 Budget, the government will continue the Kampung Angkat Madani programme.
"The government welcomes the proposal that all projects implemented under the programme should involve engagement with local MPs.
"If there are any weaknesses, please inform the Finance Ministry and the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU)," he said during question time today.

He was responding to Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong), who raised concerns over whether projects under the initiative addressed actual needs of communities and whether allocations were being used effectively.

Roslan Hashim (PN-Kulim-Bandar Baharu) also questioned the quality of work in his constituency, claiming some contractors appointed for the projects were from outside the area, adding that their work quality was disappointing.
Earlier, Liew said 221 villages had been approved under the Kampung Angkat Madani programme as of October, with RM104 million channelled towards its implementation this year.
The programme covered 43 villages in 2024 before expanding to 210 villages in 2025.

The initiative aims to improve facilities, infrastructure and community well-being by encouraging senior ministry and agency officials, as well as government-linked commpanies and government-linked investment companies, to understand local issues and develop solutions based on residents' needs.

Liew said several improvements had been introduced to improve the programme's implementation, including simplifying government procurement procedures to expedite projects and preventing multiple villages within the same parliamentary constituency from being selected.
The government had also prepared a list of priority schools for selection under the Sekolah Angkat Madani programme, based on needs involving basic infrastructure and skills development.
There are 781 schools approved in 2026, comprising 262 schools managed by government agencies and 519 supported by the corporate sector through corporate social responsibility programmes.
Liew said RM25 million had been channelled to the 262 schools managed by government agencies.
7f1ff74a7c7403c1: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman has announced that he will go on his honeymoon with singer-actress Bella Astillah after Parliament’s current sitting ends in December.

cd38cd1334118129: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman has insisted that his most important job as a husband is to keep his wife, singer and actress Bella Astillah, happy.

b8f3ee1745ef3083: LOS ANGELES: The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show returned to Los Angeles on Sunday with a celebration of the changing seasons, as the brand's signature angel-winged models swept down the runway in elaborate flower-petal, snowflake and gleaming metallic creations.
"I actually did the four seasons, and then I added in a second Winter spot," Adam Selman, the show's executive creative director, told Reuters on the pink carpet ahead of the event.

The annual runway spectacle, known for its star-studded casting, extravagant costumes and musical performances, drew celebrity guests including Lisa Rinna and Kylie Jenner.

An all-female lineup of performers, including Megan Moroney, Tate McRae, KATSEYE and Megan Thee Stallion, each embraced a distinct color palette that mirrored the night's larger fantasy theme.

The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show has traveled to cities including London, Paris, Shanghai and Cannes since its debut in 1995, but New York has remained its longtime home. That makes its return to Los Angeles a relatively rare stop for the globally watched production.
1e1d333518344b32: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) upholds the call by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, that every freedom comes with responsibility, particularly on social media.
The commission stressed that freedom of speech and the right to criticise must be exercised with courtesy and should not be used as an excuse to engage in cyberbullying.
Differences of opinion, it said, must not lead to harassment, threats, insults, personal attacks, or the dissemination of personal information that threatens an individual's safety and dignity.
"Such behaviour must not be normalised in a society that upholds freedom of speech and the values of mutual respect.

"The MCMC also takes note of His Majesty's concerns over the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) to produce fake content and the dissemination of unverified information that could incite slander and hatred," it said in a statement today.
As such, the MCMC will continue strengthening efforts to build a safe online environment through cooperation with platform providers, relevant agencies, and the public.
It added that any content suspected of violating the law will be examined and appropriate action taken under existing legal provisions.
The MCMC also urged Malaysians to heed His Majesty's call by respecting differing opinions, verifying information before sharing it, and upholding courtesy and dignity in all online interactions.
cef2c2150cf0fe50: SAMARKAND: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launches into talks on Monday with key Central Asian states before heading to India on a tour to a region with vast natural resources and China as a key competitor.
Rubio arrived in Uzbekistan's Silk Road city of Samarkand late Sunday to prepare for talks with top officials from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Uzbek hosts.
The leaders of the five former Soviet republics held talks with US President Donald Trump at the White House in November last year.

At the head of a delegation that includes 200 business executives, Rubio will visit the Samarkand's old city, a historic staging post between China and the West, before starting talks aimed at the modern-day rivalry with China.

With the United States stuck in a war with Iran and unable to halt the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Rubio has stepped up his foreign travel with recent trips to Europe and Latin America while leaving Trump to handle the conflicts and the US mid-term elections.
But Rubio insisted this week's tour is of strategic importance.
"This is an important relationship," he said shortly before his departure. "There's countries you'd like to get to because we want to build our relationships with them."
A senior State Department official told reporters on Friday that Rubio was demonstrating US goodwill towards the "deepening partnership across Central Asia", especially in the energy sector.
After Uzbekistan, Rubio will go to India where the US ambassador is Sergio Gor, who was born in Uzbekistan and is also the US special envoy for Central Asia.
The central Asian states remain linked to Russia by energy pipelines and security and migratory networks, but Russian influence has eroded since the start of its invasion of Ukraine.
And China has reaped the benefits. It is now the main trade partner of all five nations.
Chinese companies have signed a number of energy-related deals, seeking to buy natural gas in Turkmenistan, uranium in Kazakhstan and rare earths in Tajikistan.
On his second visit to India this year, Rubio will have stops in Mumbai and Jamnagar in Gujarat state. Both are major port cities.
"We're very close" to a trade deal with India, a second senior US official said of negotiations with the Asian giant that have dragged on for months.
The two sides reached a provisional agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian products.
But legal battles in US courts over Trump's tariffs have fuelled uncertainty about when a bilateral trade deal could take effect.
India-US relations were also rattled when Trump imposed 25 per cent tariffs on Indian goods in retaliation for Delhi's purchases of Russian oil, but those duties have since been lifted. --AFP

6240b09bb3f57ee7: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan sentiasa membuka ruang rayuan bantuan kepada mereka yang mengalami perubahan status kewangan, termasuk golongan pertengahan (M40) yang kehilangan pekerjaan, bagi membolehkan permohonan dinilai semula berdasarkan keadaan semasa.

Timbalan Menteri Kewangan, Liew Chin Tong, berkata mekanisme rayuan itu membolehkan penerima yang tidak lagi memenuhi syarat berdasarkan rekod terdahulu mengemukakan permohonan sekiranya situasi kewangan mereka berubah.

Beliau menjawab soalan tambahan Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) mengenai mekanisme bagi memastikan kumpulan M40 yang kehilangan pekerjaan dan mengalami kemerosotan pendapatan dinilai semula kelayakan serta bantuan bersasar mereka berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan semasa.

Selain itu, pelepasan cukai individu turut diperluas untuk rawatan perubatan meliputi perkhidmatan penjagaan selepas bersalin manakala yuran pengajian dan kemahiran diperluas meliputi semua bidang pengajian dan tuisyen anak.
Beliau menjawab soalan asal Adnan yang ingin tahu langkah membantu isi rumah M40 yang tidak lagi layak menerima bantuan bersasar tetapi terkesan dengan peningkatan kos sara hidup.
9c9fdf43e6bf29b5: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation eased to 1.8 per cent in September from 1.9 per cent in August, driven by slower price increases in housing-related costs, food and beverages, personal care and communication services.
The consumer price index (CPI) rose to 137.6 points from 135.2 points a year earlier, according to the Statistics Department.
Inflation in the housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels group moderated to 1.4 per cent from 2.1 per cent in August.
This was mainly due to slower price increases in electricity, gas and other fuels, where inflation eased sharply to 0.1 per cent from 3.3 per cent.
Inflation in water supply and miscellaneous services relating to dwellings also slowed to 1.3 per cent from 5.1 per cent.
The moderation in electricity costs followed a revision to the Automatic Fuel Adjustment rate for domestic users in Peninsular Malaysia consuming more than 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month.
The government also expanded electricity bill protection from 600kWh to 800kWh a month for domestic users between Sept 1 and Dec 31, 2026, to ease cost-of-living pressures.
In Sarawak, about 714,000 households are benefiting from a 25 per cent electricity bill discount from April to December this year.
Food and beverages inflation eased to 1.8 per cent from 1.9 per cent in August. The category accounts for 29.8 per cent of the CPI basket.

Inflation for food consumed at home slowed to 1.2 per cent from 1.4 per cent, although food consumed away from home recorded a slightly faster increase of 2.6 per cent compared with 2.5 per cent previously.

Inflation in personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services moderated to 2.8 per cent from 3.2 per cent, while information and communication eased to 1.8 per cent from 2.6 per cent.
Despite the overall moderation, transport inflation accelerated to 2.5 per cent from 2.0 per cent, driven by higher costs associated with operating personal vehicles.
Inflation in the operation of personal transport equipment subgroup rose to 2.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent.
However, inflation in public transport services eased to 7.8 per cent from 10.5 per cent.
Prices in the purchase of vehicles and transport services of goods subgroups continued to decline by 0.6 per cent and 0.5 per cent, respectively.
The department said average prices of unsubsidised fuels also increased in September.
RON97 petrol rose to RM4.64 per litre from RM4.28 in August, while diesel increased to RM5.05 from RM4.60.
The average market price of RON95 petrol climbed to RM4.16 per litre from RM3.75, compared with the subsidised price of RM1.99 per litre.
The subsidised diesel price remained at RM2.10 per litre.
Eight states and federal territories recorded inflation above the national rate of 1.8 per cent, led by Negri Sembilan and Labuan at 2.4 per cent each.
Johor, Kedah and Putrajaya recorded inflation of 2.2 per cent each, followed by Pahang at 2.1 per cent, and Selangor and Sabah at 1.9 per cent each.
On a month-on-month basis, inflation rose 0.1 per cent in September, compared with 0.3 per cent in August.
For the third quarter of 2026, inflation stood at 1.9 per cent, unchanged from the preceding quarter.
Among the categories recording higher inflation were information and communication at 2.6 per cent, followed by food and beverages and housing-related costs at 1.8 per cent each.
Recreation, sport and culture recorded inflation of 1.2 per cent, while clothing and footwear rose 0.1 per cent.

Other categories recorded slower price increases, including personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services at 3.0 per cent, restaurant and accommodation services at 2.1 per cent, and transport and education at 2.0 per cent each.
Inflation in insurance and financial services stood at 1.1 per cent.

7117f6539fe9e8d1: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's exports jumped 54.5 per cent year-on-year to RM215.1 billion in September, driven largely by strong demand for electrical and electronic (E&E) products.
The Statistics Department said E&E exports increased by RM45.1 billion from a year earlier, making them the largest contributor to export growth.
Total trade rose 53.7 per cent to RM396.5 billion, with imports climbing 52.7 per cent to RM181.4 billion.
The trade surplus widened 64.9 per cent to RM33.7 billion, marking Malaysia's 77th consecutive month of trade surplus since May 2020.
Domestic exports rose 54.7 per cent to RM162 billion, while re-exports increased 53.7 per cent to RM53.1 billion.

Besides E&E products, export growth was supported by other manufactured goods, which increased by RM14.7 billion, followed by petroleum products (RM3 billion) and optical and scientific equipment (RM2.4 billion).
The United States recorded the largest increase in Malaysian exports at RM18 billion, followed by Taiwan (RM13.7 billion) and Singapore (RM11.9 billion).
On the import side, E&E products led the increase, rising by RM42.2 billion.
Imports of machinery, equipment and parts grew by RM4.5 billion, while petroleum products increased by RM3.9 billion.
China recorded the largest increase in Malaysia's imports at RM21.1 billion, followed by Singapore (RM10.9 billion) and South Korea (RM9.1 billion).
By category, imports of intermediate goods surged 69.6 per cent to RM92.1 billion.
Capital goods imports rose 20.9 per cent to RM22.3 billion, while consumer goods increased 18.2 per cent to RM10.9 billion.
On a month-on-month basis, exports rose 12.6 per cent in September, while imports increased 11.3 per cent.
Total trade grew 12 per cent, with the trade surplus expanding 20.1 per cent, or RM5.6 billion.
For the first nine months of 2026, Malaysia's total trade increased 30.1 per cent to RM2.9 trillion from a year earlier.
In the third quarter, total trade rose 44.7 per cent year-on-year, with exports growing 46 per cent and imports increasing 43.3 per cent.
The quarterly trade surplus widened 65.1 per cent to RM84.3 billion.
3876b60768e25c4f: PETALING JAYA: The minimum age for obtaining a motorcycle licence should be raised to 18 to help curb illegal street racing among minors.

Malaysian Road Safety Research Institute (Miros) chairman Prof Dr Wong Shaw Voon said the issue of underage motorcyclists requires serious attention, as children as young as 12 are riding without a licence.
He said these minors include primary and secondary school students exposed to accident risks and illegal racing activities.
"The reality on the ground is that many minors, from primary to secondary school students, begin riding motorcycles without a licence as early as age 12.
"Therefore, the minimum age to obtain a motorcycle licence should be raised to 18 to help curb illegal racing among youths," he said.

It was reported that 'mat rempit' activities and illegal racing, including reckless motorcycle riding, are now punishable with fines up to RM10,000 following the enforcement of the Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2026.
The amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) also aim to curb "tonto" syndicate activities, alongside strengthening enforcement and digitalising Road Transport Department services.
However, Wong said that while raising the minimum age to 18 or 21 is a positive step, it will have little impact if lawbreakers are left unchecked.
He added that all parties, including parents, must play their role rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to the government.
"Many minors are already riding motorcycles without a licence as early as age 12.
"This group does not care whether the age limit is raised because they are already riding illegally. If this group is not addressed first, any age amendment will yield no results.
"Breaking the law at a young age is deeply worrying as it erodes respect for the law and authorities," he said.

Meanwhile, Chartered Institute of Logistics and Transport Malaysia (CILTM) president Prof Dr Muhammad Zaly Shah Muhammad Hussein said proposals to raise the minimum age from 16 should be studied using offender data before being treated as a primary solution.

"Raising the age limit could potentially reduce young riders' exposure to road risks if they comply. However, reducing accidents and curbing mat rempit activities are two outcomes that must be evaluated separately.
"That is why we need offender data before determining how far this measure will help. We do not yet have a sufficient basis to promise a specific percentage reduction," he said.
He added that any age limit increase must be backed by evidence showing that safety benefits outweigh the impact on educational access.
76cf88f276719927: PETALING JAYA: Semua 18 Adun Barisan Nasional (BN) Negeri Sembilan dinasihat tidak lagi campur tangan dalam hal berkaitan Dewan Keadilan dan Undangan (DKU) serta institusi diraja, kata Zahid Hamidi.

Sebelum ini, Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir menzahirkan kemurkaannya terhadap Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim dalam kejadian selepas solat Jumaat di sebuah masjid di Kuala Pilah.

Raja-raja Melayu berkata, usaha penyelesaian hendaklah diserahkan kepada pihak yang berkepentingan dan berautoriti untuk diselesaikan melalui saluran yang sah, tertib, dan berwibawa.
93430e6284f411bb: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains committed to providing assistance to Indonesia to fight fires causing the regional haze, despite preparations for the northeast monsoon, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

"Although the assets are few and the number of personnel is small compared with the overall effort to fight the fires causing the haze in Indonesia, which affects Malaysia, Singapore, Timor-Leste and Indonesia itself, we remain committed to continuing this assistance," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the Road Safety Congress 2026 here.
Zahid said Malaysia was also preparing for the northeast monsoon, which could bring another major challenge in the form of floods.
"We are now on standby to face the northeast monsoon.
"After the haze and fires, we will face a national disaster - floods," he said.

f63959964f267b4b: RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition and Iran-backed Houthis traded strikes Sunday as fighting raged in the intensifying conflict that has disturbed life for residents of the kingdom's capital Riyadh and war-wracked Yemen.

Disruption in the world's top crude oil exporter has continued to spread as the Houthis keep up their strikes, with Riyadh's landmark Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordering "mandatory" remote working until further notice for office tenants on Sunday.
No reason was given for the order, but it follows a security alert and two drone interceptions around the capital on top of waves of Houthi attacks on Saudi targets in recent weeks.
Meanwhile the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi-controlled regions of Yemen.
An alleged Saudi airstrike in northern Yemen's Saada governorate on Sunday killed at least nine people and wounded 16 others, the Houthis' Saba news agency reported.

The coalition meanwhile said Sunday that two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed in Najran near the Yemen border, while the Houthis said they "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.
The coalition blamed a "technical malfunction" for the incident, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running war with the Houthis reignited in July.

Schools in the Saudi capital and surrounding areas also extended online learning into a second week, while Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport remains closed after 13 people were killed in a major attack last week.
The Saudi coalition's decade-plus war with the Iran-backed Houthis has returned with ferocity during the US-Iran war, with regular attacks reported by both sides.
Egypt's parliament on Sunday postponed a vote on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia, two lawmakers told AFP, extending deliberations to Monday.
And Iran's newly appointed Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi threatened to inflict "enormous damage" on the United States and its allies if Washington resumes its military campaign.
- 'UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE' -
Tenants of the Kingdom Centre, which towers over central Riyadh, include financial services giant Merril Lynch, management consultancy McKinsey and the International Monetary Fund.

"Please be advised that remote working arrangements are mandatory for all office employees at Kingdom Centre, effective immediately and until further notice," the building's management said in an email seen by AFP.
The mall at the foot of the building remains open.
After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen's conflict has surged back to life and intensified when the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis have hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International airport.

A Houthi projectile injured at least six people in southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday after it struck a residential area in Najran near the border with Yemen, according to the kingdom's civil defence agency.

The coalition also said two ballistic missiles were intercepted in the kingdom's south. Threat alerts for Najran city and As Sulayyil governorate in Riyadh province were issued but quickly cancelled on Sunday.
- EGYPT SUPPORT -

The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and captured territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf's Strait of Hormuz.
On Sunday, Egypt's parliament held an emergency session after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi asked lawmakers to authorise support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.
The session was extended into Monday "to give all lawmakers the opportunity to speak and express their views", one of them told AFP.
Sisi had said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.
The hostilities were the focus of a meeting on Sunday between the Russian and Saudi foreign ministers on the sidelines of a summit between Gulf states and Russia in Bahrain's Manama.

They discussed "regional developments, particularly the escalation in Yemen, as well as the persistent threats to shipping in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab", the Saudi Foreign Ministry said on X.
Saudi Arabia's defence minister Khalid bin Salman also wrote on X that he met with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with the two discussing regional developments.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot is due to arrive in Riyadh on Sunday evening before President Emmanuel Macron's tour of the Gulf where he is expected to reaffirm Paris' support for the kingdom.--AFP

9ad6f25764216e2c: KUALA LUMPUR: Middle-income households whose members have lost their jobs can appeal for a reassessment of their eligibility for targeted government assistance, said Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong.
"Every aid recipient can submit an appeal if their existing circumstances have changed, and they can do so at any time," he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Liew was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah), who asked how the government would ensure M40 households facing unemployment or reduced incomes were not excluded from assistance because their previous earnings exceeded eligibility thresholds.
He asked whether the government had a mechanism to reassess affected households' eligibility based on current financial circumstances rather than relying on historical income records.
Liew said the government was committed to keeping the unemployment rate below four per cent.
"The unemployment rate has consistently remained, or been maintained, below four per cent. This reflects the government's commitment," he said.
In an earlier response, Liew outlined several measures under the 2027 Budget to ease the cost-of-living burden on middle-income households.
These included increasing individual tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000, reducing income tax rates for selected taxable income brackets and expanding tax relief to cover additional expenses.
The government had also introduced cash assistance and measures to ease household expenses, including electricity subsidies and Rahmah Madani sales programmes.
Liew said the government wanted to ensure that the middle-income group continued to benefit from its initiatives.
Separately, he said the government had data on the M40 group, adding that its long-term aspiration was to expand the middle-income segment until it became larger than the B40 group.

93ffc8eb40a76e4e: KUALA LUMPUR: S. Sivasangari is on the right track to challenge for a podium finish at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics after climbing to a career-high No. 4 in the latest PSA world rankings released today.

Sivasangari, who retained her Asian Games title in Aichi-Nagoya last month to qualify for LA 2028, is only the second Malaysian woman to break into the world's top four after Datuk Nicol David, who spent 108 months at No. 1.
The 27-year-old has made tremendous progress since starting training under coach Gregory Gaultier in Prague last year.
She has recorded several memorable victories under Gaultier, including wins over world No. 1 Amina Orfi, world No. 2 Hania El Hammamy and world No. 3 Nour El Sherbini.
With 17 PSA Tour titles to her name, Sivasangari could climb further up the rankings if she maintains her current form.
She pushed Hania to five games in last week's Diamond-level Egyptian Open semi-finals, only to lose 12-10 in the decider.
However, the Malaysian must now take the next step by reaching the finals of higher-tier tournaments consistently if she is to make further breakthroughs.
Former Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia (SRAM) coaching director Major (rtd) S. Maniam said he was delighted with her progress.
"I am extremely happy and proud of Sivasangari's achievements.

"Her rise to world No. 4 is a tremendous milestone and a testament to her hard work, dedication and determination, especially after recovering from injuries following a near-fatal car accident a few years ago.
"To become only the second Malaysian woman, after Nicol David, to reach a career-high ranking of world No. 4 is something she and the entire nation can be proud of."
Maniam said Sivasangari had also developed more weapons, particularly in attack.
"She has always been good in defensive play, and now, she has matched that with her attacking prowess.
"I believe she has the potential to break into the world's top three and eventually challenge for the No. 1 ranking.
"The next step is to deliver consistent performances against the world's best.
"Reaching the top is, of course, difficult, but sustaining that level requires even greater consistency.
"She just needs to make the right decisions during crucial matches against top players."
Sivasangari, who won the Australian Open and Grasshopper Cup this year, will next compete in the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City, United States, which begins tomorrow.
The Malaysian, who received a first-round bye, is the third seed.

cfd0f08e0848512b: SINGAPORE — A Singapore air safety investigation has found that turbulence can strike aircraft even when they maintain the recommended distance above storm clouds, following an incident in November 2025 that injured five cabin crew members on a Singapore Airlines (SIA) flight, The Straits Times reported.

The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB), in a report dated Oct 5, said the incident highlighted how convective activity could extend beyond the tops of storm clouds detected by weather radars, exposing aircraft to turbulence despite recommended weather avoidance margins.
According tot the report, the incident occurred on Nov 14, 2025, when flight SQ919, an Airbus A350-900 travelling from Manila to Singapore, encountered turbulence at about 7.53pm.
One cabin crew member suffered a fractured right ankle while four others sustained minor injuries.
The pilots had detected storm clouds about 80 nautical miles ahead while cruising at 40,000ft.

The English daily reported that, they estimated the clouds were at about 30,000ft and continued along their planned route, keeping the aircraft 10,000ft above them, exceeding the manufacturer’s recommended vertical separation of 5,000ft.
The pilots switched on the “fasten seat belt” signs as a precaution and advised cabin crew to continue service cautiously.
When air traffic control later instructed them to descend to 34,000ft, they opted for a slower descent of 700ft per minute to maintain greater separation from the storm clouds.
Despite these precautions, the aircraft encountered turbulence while descending at about 38,450ft.
Flight data recorded rapid changes in vertical acceleration, which fell from plus 1G to plus 0.7G in 1.34 seconds before rising to plus 1.89G in 0.34 second.
According to The Straits Times the acceleration then fluctuated before dropping to plus 0.24G, with the aircraft returning to stable flight after several seconds.
The pilot told investigators that the plane was not flying through storm clouds when the turbulence struck.
The TSIB report noted that the pilots had reviewed pre-flight briefing materials forecasting occasional storm clouds reaching heights of 51,000ft. The aircraft landed safely in Singapore at 8.41pm.
In response to queries, SIA said it acknowledged the findings and that its pilots and cabin crew received regular training, guidance and safety updates on managing turbulence.
The cabin crew member who suffered the fractured ankle has since returned to flying duties.
f321aea78c1e5560: GEORGE TOWN: The federal government has approved RM33.22 billion for 280 development projects in Penang under the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) 2027 of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).

423408a4247faf89: SINGAPORE, Oct 19 — A 38-year-old man is slated to be charged tomorrow after he allegedly stole a box containing cash-filled red packets from a hotel wedding reception in Singapore, The Straits Times reported.

593757771a2c52d3: KUALA LUMPUR: Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) sedang meneliti mekanisme untuk memperluas sekatan umur kepada pengguna platform permainan dalam talian seperti Roblox bagi meningkatkan keselamatan, khususnya kanak-kanak.

“Ayob Khan sebut itu turut merangkumi anak-anak bawah umur. Jadi, waktu ini pihak SKMM sedang mengenakan sekatan umur kepada pengguna media sosial dan kita akan teliti kesesuaian untuk mengembangkan aspek pengesahan identiti pengguna secara digital (eKYC) dan pengesahan umur kepada platform seperti Roblox,” katanya.
Beliau berkata demikian pada sidang media selepas menyaksikan majlis pertukaran dokumen pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion untuk Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB).
Fahmi berkata kerajaan melalui Majlis Keselamatan Negara (MKN) turut memantau platform terbabit.
Semalam, Ayob Khan mendedahkan kanak-kanak seawal usia 12 tahun direkrut golongan ekstremis menerusi permainan dalam talian seperti Roblox.

Ayob Khan dilaporkan berkata golongan ekstremis akan mendekati kanak-kanak menerusi platform permainan untuk berkawan sebelum membawa mereka menyertai kumpulan tertutup, di mana mereka diasuh dan dididik untuk melancarkan serangan.

Roblox sendiri telah memperkenalkan sistem akaun berasaskan umur bagi pengguna bawah 16 tahun, iaitu Roblox Kids untuk kanak-kanak berusia lima hingga lapan tahun dan Roblox Select bagi mereka berusia sembilan hingga 15 tahun.
Sistem itu dilancarkan secara global pada Jun lalu dengan kawalan kandungan dan komunikasi berbeza mengikut usia.
Bagi pengguna berusia lima hingga lapan tahun, akses dihadkan kepada permainan dengan tahap kandungan minimum atau ringan, manakala fungsi komunikasi dinyahaktifkan secara lalai.

Pengguna berusia sembilan hingga 15 tahun pula menggunakan akaun Roblox Select yang membenarkan akses kepada kandungan sehingga tahap sederhana, dengan kawalan komunikasi dan tetapan ibu bapa mengikut usia.

Pengguna berusia 16 dan 17 tahun yang melepasi pemeriksaan umur boleh mengakses kandungan lebih matang, termasuk permainan berklasifikasi 16+, manakala pengguna berusia 18 tahun ke atas boleh mengakses permainan terhad selepas melengkapkan pengesahan umur.

Dalam perkembangan lain, Fahmi berkata pembiayaan bernilai RM5.2 bilion untuk DNB dijangka memperkukuh kedudukan kewangan syarikat itu, sekali gus menyokong kelangsungan operasi dan pembangunan rangkaian 5G negara.
Katanya, pencapaian itu mencerminkan keyakinan sektor perbankan terhadap masa depan DNB, selain kepentingan infrastruktur telekomunikasi dalam memacu ekonomi digital negara.
Beliau berkata rangkaian 5G yang kini mencapai liputan 82.4% kawasan berpenduduk perlu terus diperkasa bagi memenuhi keperluan industri dan pengguna.
